title: Genetics and molecular biology
stage: College neuroscience and cognitive science degree
audience: a college student in a neuroscience, cognitive science, psychology or biology degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Analyze inheritance and pedigrees, linkage, chromosomes, mutation and repair, transcription, translation and gene regulation, molecular tools, genomics, population genetics and the genetics of complex traits and cancer.

weeks.8: Gene regulation in eukaryotes and epigenetics
weeks.9: Molecular tools: PCR, sequencing and cloning
weeks.12: Genetics of complex traits and cancer

blocks.deliverable: Determine the inheritance pattern of a pedigree and compute a map distance.
Explain how a repair defect raises cancer risk.
Predict the effect of splice-site and nonsense mutations.
Week 7 midterm; explain the lac operon and DNA methylation.
Design PCR primers and read a sequence alignment.
Compare a polygenic risk score with a single-gene test.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Pedigree and variant analysis: analyze a supplied family pedigree and sequence variant, state the inheritance pattern, and estimate recurrence risks.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
